PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[Redacted Hospital] NHS Foundation Trust
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient: [Redacted name]
Date of Birth: [Redacted DOB]
Hospital Number: [Redacted ID]
Maternal Age: 27 years
Gestation: 13 weeks (by ultrasound dating)
Sample Type: Chorionic villi
Sample Date: [Redacted date]
Report Date: [Redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Referral Reason: Prenatal testing at 13 weeks gestation
Clinical Context: Haemoglobinopathy testing requested
Family History: Not provided

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescent PCR (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection
Target chromosomes: 13, 18, and 21
Sample: Uncultured chorionic villi

METHODOLOGY
DNA extraction from uncultured chorionic villus sample followed by multiplex PCR amplification of highly polymorphic short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. Fluorescently labeled primers used for detection on capillary electrophoresis system. Peak height ratios analyzed to determine chromosome copy number.

STR markers analyzed:
- Chromosome 13: D13S305, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S386, D18S535
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S11

RESULTS

Chromosome 13 Analysis:
D13S305: Normal disomic pattern (1:1 ratio)
D13S628: Normal disomic pattern (1:1 ratio)
Result: Normal chromosome 13 complement

Chromosome 18 Analysis:
D18S386: Normal disomic pattern (1:1 ratio)
D18S535: Normal disomic pattern (1:1 ratio)
Result: Normal chromosome 18 complement

Chromosome 21 Analysis:
D21S1435: Normal disomic pattern (1:1 ratio)
D21S11: Normal disomic pattern (1:1 ratio)
Result: Normal chromosome 21 complement

OVERALL RESULT: rsa(13,18,21)x2
Normal chromosome complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21
No abnormalities detected

INTERPRETATION
The QF-PCR analysis shows normal disomic patterns for all tested markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. This result indicates no evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in the analyzed chorionic villus sample.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
No evidence of trisomy for chromosomes 13, 18, or 21 in the fetal sample. This result provides reassurance regarding the most common autosomal trisomies.

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis planned based on current results.

LIMITATIONS
This test specifically analyzes chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only. It does not detect:
- Other chromosomal abnormalities (sex chromosome aneuploidies, structural rearrangements)
- Mosaicism below 20% level
- Segmental imbalances or microdeletions/duplications
- Single gene disorders
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be completely excluded

If clinical suspicion remains for other chromosomal abnormalities, conventional karyotyping or chromosomal microarray analysis should be considered.

Authorized by: Dr [Redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
Contact: [Redacted phone] for queries
